title.value: Continual Learning In Environments With Polynomial Mixing Times
title.justification: The title of the paper clearly indicates its focus on "Continual Learning In Environments With Polynomial Mixing Times" as the central topic.
title.quote: Continual Learning In Environments With Polynomial Mixing Times

extractions.description: The paper explores the concept of mixing times in Markov chains and their impact on continual reinforcement learning (RL). It introduces the formalism of scalable Markov decision processes (MDPs) and demonstrates through empirical analysis how polynomial mixing times can emerge and lead to unstable learning behavior in RL. The paper also provides theoretical insights into the scalability of MDPs and the challenges posed by myopic bias and stale bootstrapped estimates when dealing with large-scale problems in RL.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development themes. It centers around theoretical and empirical studies in continual reinforcement learning, particularly related to Markov decision processes and mixing times.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The mixing time of the Markov chain induced by a policy limits performance in real-world continual learning scenarios. Yet, the effect of mixing times on learning in continual reinforcement learning (RL) remains underexplored.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific category related to climate or ecological sustainable development. Its primary focus is on reinforcement learning and Markov decision processes.
primary_category.quote: Continual reinforcement learning (RL) [1] is an aspirational field of research confronting the difficulties of long-term, real-world applications by studying problems of increasing scale, diversity, and non-stationarity.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development, given its primary focus on continual learning in reinforcement learning.
secondary_categories.quote: Here, we address this meta-challenge by formalizing RL problems that vary in size and by analyzing the scaling behavior of popular RL algorithms.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category of sustainable development applies as the paper focuses on Markov chains and continual learning in RL rather than any sustainable development issues.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose the formalism of scalable MDPs in Definition 1 to characterize an abstract class of MDPs where the MDPs within the class are differentiated based on a changing scale parameter.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no applicable sub-categories as the paper does not touch on sustainable development topics.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our analysis demonstrates both that polynomial mixing times do emerge in practice and how their existence may lead to unstable learning behavior like catastrophic forgetting in continual learning settings.

applications.justification: The paper investigates issues related to continual reinforcement learning, specifically addressing mixing times and their impact on learning, which can affect long-term learning strategies.
applications.quote: In this paper, we characterize problems that are of long-term interest to the development of continual RL, which we call scalable MDPs, through the lens of mixing times.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not necessitate the creation of a new sustainable development category as it does not focus on or contribute to this area.
new_primary_category.quote: The practical requirement for researchers to work on problems of reasonable complexity in the short-term presents a meta-challenge: choosing the right small-scale problems so that the approaches we develop scale up to the use cases of the future.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is necessary as the paper is not aligned with sustainable development initiatives.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Theoretical insights combined with empirical analysis form the basis of our study into the effects of polynomial mixing times on continual reinforcement learning.
